stem: A 70-kg healthy 25-year-old man has about 42 liters of total body water. Which of the following best estimates the distribution of this water between his intracellular fluid and his plasma?

options.label: A
options.text: About 17 liters intracellular and about 8 liters as plasma
options.misconception: The two compartments' shares are being swapped and plasma overestimated.
options.explanation: The larger share is intracellular (about 60 percent), and plasma is only a fifth of the extracellular third — far less than 8 liters.

options.label: B
options.text: About 25 liters intracellular and about 17 liters as plasma
options.misconception: The whole extracellular compartment is being counted as plasma.
options.explanation: The 17-liter extracellular volume is mostly interstitial fluid; plasma is only about 20 percent of the ECF, roughly 3 liters.

options.label: C
options.text: About 25 liters intracellular and about 3 liters as plasma
options.misconception: None; ICF is ~60% of body water and plasma ~20% of the ECF.
options.explanation: The ICF holds about 60 percent of total body water (~25 L here). The ECF holds the remaining third (~17 L), and only about 20 percent of the ECF is plasma (~3 L), the rest being interstitial fluid.

options.label: D
options.text: About 10 liters intracellular and about 10 liters as plasma
options.misconception: The compartments are being split evenly, contrary to their measured proportions.
options.explanation: Body water is not evenly divided: the ICF predominates at about 60 percent, while plasma is a small fraction (about 20 percent) of the extracellular third.

options.label: E
options.text: About 42 liters intracellular and about 1 liter as plasma
options.misconception: Total body water is being equated with the intracellular compartment.
options.explanation: Total body water splits roughly 60/40 between intracellular and extracellular fluid; the intracellular share is about 25 liters, not the entire 42.

context: Learning objective: partition body water. ICF ≈ 60% of total body water; ECF ≈ one-third; plasma ≈ 20% of ECF (the rest interstitial).
imageCaption: Countercurrent multiplier, inulin=GFR, fluid compartments, EPO, micturition.
